items.title: Donetsk mayor reports teenager wounded in Ukrainian drone attack
items.summary: Donetsk Mayor Alexei Kulemzin said a teenager born in 2012 was injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on the city's Petrovsky district on Sunday. He also reported damaged windows at a medical facility in the Budyonnovsky district during overnight attacks.

items.title: Ukrainian drones reportedly strike oil storage tanks in Tatarstan
items.summary: Ukrainian drones reportedly attacked oil storage tanks in Russia's Tatarstan region, with emergency services responding to the aftermath. The report did not specify the facility, the extent of damage or any casualties.

items.title: Russian military expert claims bridge strikes have disrupted Ukrainian logistics
items.summary: Russian military analyst Andrey Marochko claimed strikes on bridges over the Dnipro have substantially reduced Ukrainian military traffic toward Donbas and Russian-controlled southern territories. He also asserted that only three of Kyiv's six bridges remain fully operational.

items.title: Russia claims strikes on Izmail port and military rail transport
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces struck port infrastructure in Izmail allegedly used for military deliveries, two locomotives near the Dniprodzerzhynsk railway station and a cargo ship southwest of Odesa allegedly carrying military supplies. The ministry did not provide detailed damage assessments.

items.title: Russia says air defences intercepted 192 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said air defences shot down 192 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions during the night. The ministry's figure describes claimed interceptions and does not establish how many drones were launched or whether any struck targets.

items.title: FSB says man detained in Crimea over alleged intelligence sharing with Ukraine
items.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service said it detained a man in Crimea accused of passing information about a former Donetsk security ministry employee to Ukrainian military intelligence for an alleged assassination plot. The accusation is an account of the agency's allegation, not a judicial finding.

items.title: Japanese visitors to Donetsk reportedly added to Ukraine's Myrotvorets database
items.summary: A Japanese delegation that visited Russian-controlled Donetsk has reportedly been added to the Myrotvorets website, including a lawmaker named Fujimoto and journalist Iizuka. The listing follows a separate diplomatic dispute over Italian politicians appearing in the database.

items.title: Medvedev outlines circumstances in which Russia could use nuclear weapons
items.summary: Russian Security Council deputy chairman Dmitry Medvedev wrote that Russia had not used nuclear weapons in the Ukraine conflict because it saw no direct necessity. He argued that covert Western transfers of nuclear weapons to Kyiv could justify a preemptive Russian nuclear strike, and said any such decision would follow a comprehensive assessment.

items.title: Odesa reportedly left without power, heating and water after weekend strikes
items.summary: Odesa's military administration chief, Serhiy Lysak, said damage to energy facilities over the weekend had left the city without electricity, heating and water. Public transport reportedly stopped operating because of the power outage.

items.title: Bryansk governor reports civilian killed in Ukrainian drone attack
items.summary: A regional governor said a 65-year-old man was killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on the village of Brakhlov in Russia's Bryansk region. The report gave no additional details about damage or other casualties.

items.title: Le Pen warns direct NATO intervention in Ukraine could trigger world war
items.summary: French politician Marine Le Pen said direct NATO entry into the Ukraine conflict would lead to a third world war. She described a prolonged conflict or a broader recognition of its consequences as alternative scenarios.

items.title: Donetsk air-defence system reportedly thwarted 113 drone attacks in a week
items.summary: A report said the Donbas Dome air-defence system prevented 113 attacks over the past week, including interceptions of armed drones in Donetsk, near Shakhtarsk and in Horlivka. The figure is a reported interception total rather than a confirmed count of attempted attacks.

items.title: Estonia says EU has prepared 22nd sanctions package targeting 150 Russian entities and individuals
items.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said the European Commission has completed preparations for a 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, covering 150 people and companies. He also described a proposed Schengen entry ban as part of the measures, according to a report citing Postimees.

items.title: Report says Zelensky acknowledged Ukrainian operation against Russian ships off Libya
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent reported that President Volodymyr Zelensky attributed an attack on the Russian corvette Merkury and cargo vessel Angara near Libya to a joint operation by Ukraine's security service and armed forces involving seven Ukrainian-made unmanned boats. The account adds a reported statement of responsibility to earlier coverage of the attacks.

items.title: Donetsk mayor says two women injured in overnight drone attack on Mospyne
items.summary: Donetsk Mayor Alexei Kulemzin said a woman born in 1969 and a young woman born in 2007 were injured in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack on Mospyne. He said both received medical treatment and separately reported renewed drone attacks on Donetsk with air defences operating.

items.title: German media report Western concern over possible Russian nuclear-armed satellite launch
items.summary: An investigation attributed to German broadcasters WDR and NDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung says Western intelligence agencies are assessing whether Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite called Sputnik-S by year's end. The report says NATO members exchanged intelligence on a purportedly ready system near Moscow, with a possible launch as early as December.

items.title: Russian Defence Ministry claims 819 Ukrainian drones intercepted in 24 hours
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences destroyed 819 Ukrainian drones and a HIMARS rocket over the preceding day. In its latest briefing, the ministry also claimed strikes on Ukrainian drone production and storage sites and estimated Ukrainian military losses at around 1,110 personnel.

items.title: Luhansk leader reports one killed and six wounded in Ukrainian attacks
items.summary: Leonid Pasechnik said attacks by Ukrainian forces in the Luhansk region killed one person and injured six others, including three children. The report did not specify the exact locations or weapons involved.

items.title: Kyiv official says South Bridge may remain closed through year-end
items.summary: Darnytskyi district administration head Oleksandr Kovtunov reportedly said traffic across Kyiv's South Bridge is unlikely to resume before the end of 2026 because of serious damage from Russian strikes. He gave no firm timetable for repairs.

items.title: Russian ambassador to Libya warns of response to Benghazi ship attacks
items.summary: Russian Ambassador to Libya Aidar Aganin said Moscow would consider responses to attacks on Russian vessels near Benghazi, accusing Ukraine of extending the conflict into distant maritime areas. He also alleged Western logistical and intelligence support for such operations.

items.title: EU budget negotiations face disputes over loans to Ukraine
items.summary: A report citing Politico says EU governments are skeptical of parts of the proposed 2028–2034 budget, including lending to Ukraine, agricultural subsidies and a digital tax. Officials reportedly expect difficult negotiations over the spending plan.

items.title: Russian analyst claims offensive is approaching outskirts of Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Military analyst Alexei Ramm claimed Russian forces are advancing on a broad front toward Zaporizhzhia and have approached Komyshuvakha, while Ukrainian units face pressure near Orikhiv and Omelnyk. His assessment includes claims of severe Ukrainian losses and encirclement that are not established as confirmed territorial changes.

items.title: SAPO reports court transfers 150 million hryvnias in Midas case to asset agency
items.summary: SAPO said Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court appeals chamber ordered 150 million hryvnias previously posted as bail for a former energy minister in the Midas case transferred to the national asset management agency. Prosecutors allege the money was laundered through accounts linked to a former lawmaker and a state bank; the ruling concerns management of seized assets, not a conviction.

items.title: Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery halts operations after six-hour attack, governor says
items.summary: Rostov regional governor Yuri Slyusar said the Novoshakhtinsk petroleum facility suspended operations after a combined Ukrainian drone and missile attack lasting more than six hours. Emergency crews were working to contain the consequences, with no detailed damage or casualty assessment provided.

items.title: Kremlin says Moscow plans contact with European governments over peace efforts
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia intends to initiate contact with European governments to assess their willingness to pursue peace. He also said Moscow's proposed humanitarian operation in Kostiantynivka remains on offer despite what he described as a lack of response from Kyiv.

items.title: Russia allocates nearly 47 billion rubles for Kaliningrad supply ferries
items.summary: Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin announced nearly 47 billion rubles in funding, including National Wealth Fund resources, for two railway ferries to strengthen the Ust-Luga–Baltiysk supply route by 2030. The project comes amid tensions over Baltic transit restrictions and attacks on Russian shipping.

items.title: German foreign minister calls for more equal European sharing of Ukraine aid costs
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged European allies to share the financial burden of supporting Ukraine more evenly and continue their assistance. A report citing Reuters contrasted roughly 30.8 billion euros spent by Germany with 2.6 billion euros by Spain.

items.title: SAPO announces suspicions against former Ukrainian deputy prime minister in payroll case
items.summary: SAPO said a former deputy prime minister and two ministry employees have been formally notified of suspicion over allegedly using ministry payroll funds to pay five people who actually worked as drivers and security guards. Investigators allege false employment records supported the payments between March and June 2025; the investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: Belgorod authorities report three civilians wounded in drone attacks
items.summary: Regional emergency officials said three civilians were injured in Ukrainian drone attacks in Russia's Belgorod region. The report did not identify the precise locations or provide further details on their conditions.

items.title: Dnipropetrovsk electric transit reportedly suspended amid power disruptions
items.summary: A report citing the city's transport department says trams, trolleybuses and metro services stopped in Dnipropetrovsk after traction substations lost power. The report also described Russian strikes on a 330-kilovolt substation, railway facilities and Izmail port, some of which were covered earlier.

items.title: Western-owned companies in Russia seen as leverage over frozen Russian assets
items.summary: A report says Russia has placed 16 Western-linked businesses under temporary management, leaving them operating but outside their owners' control. An economist argued that Moscow could use Western corporate assets in Russia as leverage if the EU moves to seize frozen Russian central-bank funds for Ukraine; this is an assessment of potential retaliation, not an announced confiscation.

items.title: Putin says Moscow invited European representatives to discuss security
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said Russia had invited European representatives through diplomatic channels to visit Moscow and outline their positions on security arrangements. The statement comes as Moscow seeks further engagement with European governments over the conflict.

items.title: Report details Dutch defence contracts with drone maker supplying Ukraine
items.summary: A report citing Dutch government documents says defence technology firm Destinus received a Dutch contract worth about €291.9 million for drones supplied to Ukraine this year. The company is also reportedly contracted to supply Ruta Block 2 cruise missiles to Kyiv; claims linking it to the Crimean Bridge attack come from the same report.

items.title: Horlivka official says two civilians wounded in drone strike on passenger bus
items.summary: Horlivka city head Ivan Prikhodko said updated information showed two civilians were injured when a Ukrainian drone directly struck a passenger bus in the city's Nikitovsky district on November 22.

items.title: Russia summons Estonian diplomat over planned border closures
items.summary: Moscow summoned Estonia's chargé d'affaires following Tallinn's decision to close its remaining border crossings with Russia from December 1. Russian officials criticized the measure as confrontational, while Estonia has alleged Russian involvement in an attempted attack on a defence-industry facility.

items.title: Finnish lawmakers propose border fortifications drawing on Ukraine war
items.summary: Finnish lawmakers are reportedly proposing anti-tank ditches, barriers and other fortifications along the Russian border, drawing lessons from the war in Ukraine. Parliamentary defence committee head Heikki Autto emphasized the difficulty of recovering territory once lost.

items.title: Russia accuses Estonia of allowing Ukrainian drones to cross its airspace
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry alleged that Estonia has quietly permitted Ukrainian drones to use its airspace for attacks on northwestern Russia. The ministry's accusation did not include publicly detailed evidence in the reported statement.

items.title: European Commission rejects bilateral security consultations with Russia
items.summary: The European Commission declined Moscow's invitation for a European delegation to discuss security arrangements in Russia, according to a report citing the Commission. It reportedly prefers talks concerning Ukraine in a multilateral format rather than bilateral consultations with Moscow.

items.title: Ukrainian naval drones reportedly hit Iranian vessel off Libya
items.summary: A report alleges that Ukrainian naval drones struck the Iranian vessel Alvan in Libyan territorial waters, following attacks on Russian ships near Benghazi. The report did not provide a damage assessment or an official Ukrainian statement accepting responsibility for this particular attack.

items.title: Four DTEK energy facilities reportedly damaged in Dnipropetrovsk region
items.summary: Ukrainian media reportedly said repeated strikes damaged equipment and caused fires at four DTEK energy facilities over two days. The report said around 353,000 homes lost power, including in Dnipro, Novomoskovsk and surrounding areas.

items.title: Donetsk authorities report two civilians killed and 26 wounded over a week
items.summary: The regional human rights commissioner's office said attacks attributed to Ukrainian forces killed two civilians and injured 26 others in the Donetsk region over the preceding week. The figures are the office's reported weekly toll.

items.title: Russian drone strike reportedly hits central Kyiv near government quarter
items.summary: A report attributed to Financial Times journalist Christopher Miller described a Russian drone strike near Ukraine's presidential office and Maidan in central Kyiv, with fire and black smoke visible. Other posts reported strikes in the city, but gave no casualty assessment.

items.title: Odesa could face up to three weeks of power disruption after strikes
items.summary: A report citing Forbes Ukraine says damage to three pylons on a power line from the South Ukraine nuclear power plant could leave Odesa without electricity for up to three weeks. The reported repair outlook adds detail to earlier coverage of widespread outages.

items.title: Merz says Europe is ready for talks with Russia on Baltic security
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz reportedly said Europe is prepared to negotiate with Russia and called for intensive talks on Baltic Sea security to prevent escalation. His remarks follow differing European positions on the format of talks with Moscow.

items.title: Russia claims strike on arms-carrying locomotive near Merefa
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces struck a railway locomotive near Merefa in Kharkiv region, alleging it was being used to transport weapons. The ministry provided no independent damage assessment in the report.

items.title: NATO reconnaissance aircraft reportedly flies seven hours near Ukraine
items.summary: An air traffic control source cited in a Russian report said a Bombardier ARTEMIS II reconnaissance aircraft spent more than seven hours over the Black Sea region, making turns over Romania near the Ukrainian border. The report did not allege an airspace violation.

items.title: EU outlines proposed sanctions on 60 more Russian banks and energy services
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen outlined proposed restrictions including disconnecting another 60 Russian banks from SWIFT, curbs on payment and cryptocurrency platforms, and bans on servicing Russian energy infrastructure. The package also proposes entry restrictions for former Russian military personnel and limits on Russian participation in European sporting events; EU member states must approve the measures.

items.title: Salvini reportedly threatens to block Ukraine military aid over Myrotvorets listings
items.summary: Italian Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini reportedly demanded the removal of Italian citizens from Ukraine's Myrotvorets database and an apology for his own listing. He threatened to block further military assistance to Ukraine unless the issue is addressed.

items.title: Zelensky says reparations are needed to overcome hostility between Ukrainians and Russians
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said deep hostility between Ukrainians and Russians stems from Russia's invasion and argued that reparations are necessary to overcome it. His remarks came in response to a journalist's question about relations between the two populations.

items.title: Former Ukrainian security officer alleges intelligence links to drug trafficking
items.summary: Former SBU colonel Roman Chervinsky reportedly accused elements of Ukraine's military intelligence and security services of protecting a drug trafficking network during the war, and raised allegations concerning an attempted assassination of a businessman in Monaco. These are his allegations, not established findings of an investigation.

items.title: Estonian prime minister says further Baltic Sea attacks on Russian ships are possible
items.summary: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal reportedly said incidents like the attack on the Russian cargo vessel Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland could recur, and that Ukrainian targeting of Russian ships in the Baltic Sea was not surprising. The comments come amid heightened tensions over maritime attacks.

items.title: Zaporizhzhia reportedly suffers major electricity disruptions after strike
items.summary: A report described the aftermath of a strike on the outskirts of Zaporizhzhia and serious power disruptions in the city. It did not provide casualty figures or a detailed assessment of the damaged infrastructure.

items.title: Officials report oil storage damage in Tatarstan and industrial strike in Perm
items.summary: Regional authorities reportedly acknowledged damage to oil storage facilities near Almetyevsk in Tatarstan and an industrial site in Perm Krai after Ukrainian drone attacks. No casualties were reported in either region, while other overnight strikes affected several Russian regions.

items.title: Finnish defence official says Ukraine likely behind Baltic Sea ship attack
items.summary: Finnish Defence Forces communications director Colonel Huhtinen said Ukraine was most likely responsible for an attack on a Russian vessel in the Baltic Sea, according to Yle. He said the reason for targeting the ship was unknown.

items.title: Ukrainian lawmaker reportedly confronted by mobilisation officers
items.summary: A report alleges that mobilisation officers grabbed lawmaker Oleksandr Kunitsky and took his phone after he intervened during an attempt to detain a passer-by. The officers reportedly backed off after recognising him as a member of parliament; the account does not establish an official finding of misconduct.

items.title: Donetsk energy official promises further assistance to restore power and heating
items.summary: Deputy energy minister Alexander Putyakov said residents would eventually have electricity and heating restored, while asking for patience. He said additional federal assistance was expected soon amid disruptions attributed to Ukrainian attacks.

items.title: Russian military report describes contested fighting near Lyman
items.summary: A Russian battlefield account claims its forces regained territory north of Torske and resumed attacks in woodland northwest of Zarichne. It also describes unsettled positions around Dibrova, Yampil and Ozerne, with fighting continuing and no stable frontline established in nearby forest.

items.title: Russia claims 87 Ukrainian drones intercepted across several regions
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said air defences destroyed 87 Ukrainian drones over regions including Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk, Oryol, Perm, Crimea and Tatarstan, as well as the Black Sea. The figure is the ministry's reported interception count.

items.title: Libyan official says Benghazi port attack injured civilians and damaged property
items.summary: Libya's Presidential Council deputy chairman Musa al-Koni said the attack on Benghazi's seaport caused material damage and civilian injuries. He described Ukraine's actions as tantamount to a declaration of war, following reports that Kyiv accepted responsibility for an attack at the port.

items.title: Ukraine's defence minister says Russia produces a ballistic missile every five hours
items.summary: Ukraine's defence minister said Russia is producing roughly one ballistic missile every five hours and continues to increase its production rate. The statement highlights Kyiv's concern about Russia's capacity to sustain long-range strikes.

items.title: Zelensky warns Russia is preparing another large-scale attack
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian security services have informed him that Russia is preparing another massive attack on Ukraine. He did not specify a date or intended targets in the reported remarks.

items.title: Ukrainian farmers face growing bankruptcy risk as exports decline
items.summary: A report citing Bloomberg says Ukrainian farmers could face bankruptcies by spring as financial reserves run out, unsold grain depresses local prices and banks restrict lending. Grain exports reportedly fell by about a third this season, while fuel and fertilizer costs and Russian attacks on processing facilities add pressure.

items.title: Russia claims strike on cargo ship east of Odesa and military railway locomotive
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces struck a dry cargo vessel in the Black Sea east of Odesa that it alleged was delivering dual-use goods for Ukrainian forces. It also claimed a strike on a locomotive used to transport weapons and military equipment.

items.title: Libya prepares international court case over Benghazi port strikes
items.summary: Libya's embassy in The Hague said it is preparing documents for a case against Ukraine at the International Court of Justice over reported strikes on Benghazi port. The Libyan Foreign Ministry also requested an official explanation from Kyiv, while Presidential Council member Musa al-Koni called for UN Security Council action.

items.title: Rutte urges NATO countries to prepare civilian services for possible war
items.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte urged governments, businesses and citizens to strengthen readiness for a potential conflict, speaking at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin. He emphasized keeping electricity, heating, hospitals, transport and communications operating amid threats he linked to Russia and its partners.

items.title: Merz proposes renewed Ukraine peace talks involving Europe, Russia and US
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said adviser-level talks involving Ukraine, Russia, Europe and the United States should resume soon, potentially in Abu Dhabi. He said the proposed discussions had been coordinated with Washington.

items.title: Zelensky asks US for Patriot missiles amid warning of further Russian strikes
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to the United States to provide Patriot air-defence missiles, citing Ukrainian intelligence about preparations for new Russian attacks. The appeal adds a specific request for air-defence supplies to his earlier warning of a possible major strike.

items.title: AfD co-leader says party would halt German payments and weapons deliveries to Ukraine
items.summary: Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel said her party would stop German payments and arms deliveries to Ukraine if it came to power. She also called for cuts to defence spending and Germany's contributions to the European Union; these are party proposals, not current government policy.
